name: Côtes d'Auvergne

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this cool ripen Müller-Thurgau, Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer, Riesling and Pinot Noir fully without cooking off their freshness.
Most rain falls while the vines grow. Damp leaves invite mildew and rot, so growers spray more and pick carefully.

soil.rock: Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 4°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Only very early grapes ripen well, mostly hybrids and a few vinifera.
